subject.title: refactor(mac): make app node a CLI capability superset

question: After the two correctness defects are repaired, should the app-owned private CLI worker become the canonical execution, approval, filesystem, plugin, skill, and MCP runtime for Mac nodes?
rationale: This permanently moves privileged behavior across a new process and ownership boundary; tests can verify mechanics, but a feature/security owner must confirm that the boundary and required signed-app proof are acceptable.

options.title: Approve after repair and proof
options.body: Adopt the worker architecture after preserving current Mac contracts and attaching inspectable signed-app boundary evidence.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Land only transport-independent runtime extraction and defer app integration until broader upgrade and security proof is available.

options.title: Retain native ownership
options.body: Keep the duplicate Swift paths and close this implementation direction if the cross-process boundary is not acceptable.

recommendation.title: Approve after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Adopt the worker architecture after preserving current Mac contracts and attaching inspectable signed-app boundary evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature proposal and recent merged Mac node, native capability, and approval history make this the strongest available product and boundary owner.
